CODE
229
A divorce is pronounced when the judge finds that the spouses are irretrievably estranged. Disunion is irremediable when it makes it reasonably impossible for the spouses to continue living together or to resume doing so. Proof of irretrievable separation may be provided by any legal means.
Irretrievable separation is established when the application is made jointly by the two spouses after more than six months of de facto separation or when it is repeated twice in accordance with Article 1255, ¤ 1, of the Judicial Code.
It is also established when the application is made by only one spouse after more than one year of de facto separation or when it is repeated on two occasions in accordance with Article 1255, ¤ 2, of the Judicial Code.
